title: COUNT Recalculation on THIS_AND_FUTURE Edit Relative to Original RECURRENCE-ID Slot

citations.verbatim_quote: The COUNT rule part defines the number of occurrences at which to range-bound the recurrence. The "DTSTART" property value always counts as the first occurrence.

The "RANGE" parameter is used to specify the effective range of recurrence instances from the instance specified by the "RECURRENCE-ID" property value. The value for the range parameter can only be "THISANDFUTURE" to indicate a range defined by the given recurrence instance and all subsequent instances. Subsequent instances are determined by their "RECURRENCE-ID" value and not their current scheduled start time. Subsequent instances defined in separate components are not impacted by the given recurrence instance. When the given recurrence instance is rescheduled, all subsequent instances are also rescheduled by the same time difference.

rationale: Under RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10, COUNT bounds the total number of occurrences of a recurrence rule with DTSTART counting as the first occurrence, and per Section 3.8.5.1 (and the worked example in RFC 5546 Section 4.4.1), COUNT is evaluated on the RRULE candidate stream before EXDATE subtraction and independently of RDATE additions. Under Section 3.8.4.4, the split boundary for THISANDFUTURE is determined by the RECURRENCE-ID value (the original occurrence time of the split instance), NOT by the newly rescheduled start time. When a COUNT-bounded series of `N` RRULE occurrences is split at `recurrence_id` with THIS_AND_FUTURE range without an explicit replacement `rrule` in the edit patch, `k` candidate RRULE occurrences (before EXDATE subtraction and excluding RDATE-only occurrences) occurred strictly prior to the original `recurrence_id` timestamp (`occurrence_dt < split_orig_dtstart`). To preserve the total RRULE candidate count `N` across the split series, the forked future series' inherited `COUNT` must be decremented by `k` (yielding `N - k` RRULE candidate occurrences in the future segment), regardless of whether the edit reschedules the split occurrence to a later or earlier time on that day. Conversely, when the edit patch explicitly provides a new `rrule` (with its own `COUNT`, `UNTIL`, or unbounded rule), that explicit `rrule` defines the recurrence schedule of the future series directly and its `COUNT` MUST be respected as specified without subtracting `k`.
store_implication: When determining the future component's `rrule.count` during a THIS_AND_FUTURE split edit (where `recurrence_id` is not None): (1) If `rrule` is explicitly provided in the edit patch, preserve the caller's explicit `rrule` (including any specified `COUNT`) without subtracting prior occurrences. (2) If `rrule` is inherited from the prior segment (omitted in the edit patch) and has a `COUNT` bound: (a) the cutoff timestamp MUST be the original occurrence date/time parsed from `recurrence_id` and aligned with the prior component's `dtstart` timezone (if parsed as a naive datetime while the prior component's `dtstart` is timezone-aware), and MUST NOT be the rescheduled `dtstart` of the edited component; (b) for each prior candidate occurrence generated by the inherited RRULE strictly before that original `recurrence_id` timestamp (`dtvalue < split_orig_dtstart`, evaluated before `EXDATE` subtraction and excluding `RDATE`-only occurrences), the future component's `rrule.count` is decremented by 1 (`max(1, N - k)`). When `rrule` is inherited and no `EXDATE`s or `RDATE`s apply, the sum of occurrences emitted on the expanded timeline by the truncated prior series (`k`) and the forked future series (`N - k`) equals `N`.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Rescheduling to a later time on the same day (e.g., 09:00 moved to 11:00 on 2025-05-06 for a daily series with COUNT=3 starting 2025-05-05 09:00): comparing prior occurrences against the new rescheduled start time (11:00) erroneously treats BOTH 2025-05-05 09:00 and 2025-05-06 09:00 as prior occurrences, decrementing COUNT from 3 to 1 instead of 2 and losing the 2025-05-07 occurrence.

Rescheduling to an earlier time or date before the original slot (e.g., moving the 2025-05-06 09:00 occurrence to 2025-05-06 07:00): comparing against the new start time would stop before the original slot if another occurrence existed between 07:00 and 09:00.

Explicit replacement RRULE with COUNT in patch (e.g., splitting a daily COUNT=4 series at the 3rd occurrence while passing `rrule='FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=3'`): subtracting `k=2` prior occurrences from the caller's explicit `COUNT=3` would corrupt the new weekly rule to `COUNT=1`; explicit `rrule` patches must keep `COUNT=3`.

Editing without an explicit new `dtstart` on a timezone-aware series: if the parsed `recurrence_id` is not aligned with the master `dtstart` timezone before comparing against timezone-aware recurrence instances, datetime comparison fails due to mixing naive and timezone-aware datetimes.

scenarios.name: edit_this_and_future_reschedule_later_time_preserves_count
scenarios.description: Rescheduling the second occurrence (May 6 09:00) of a 3-day timezone-aware series to 11:00 with THIS_AND_FUTURE range decrements COUNT by 1 (to 2), preserving May 5 (09:00), May 6 (11:00), and May 7 (11:00).

scenarios.name: edit_this_and_future_with_prior_exdate_and_rdate_counts_rrule_candidates_only
scenarios.description: Splitting a COUNT=4 daily series at May 3 (3rd RRULE occurrence) when May 2 is excluded via EXDATE and an extra RDATE exists on May 1 15:00 decrements COUNT by k=2 (the 2 prior RRULE candidates on May 1 and May 2, ignoring the RDATE-only occurrence and counting the EXDATE-excluded RRULE slot) to COUNT=2.

scenarios.name: edit_this_and_future_with_explicit_rrule_count_preserves_new_count
scenarios.description: Splitting a COUNT=4 daily series at May 3 (after 2 prior occurrences) while explicitly specifying rrule='FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=3' in the patch preserves COUNT=3 on the forked future series without subtracting the 2 prior occurrences.

Contextual RFC check (+/- 40 lines): Verified RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10 (L2312-L2314) and Section 3.8.4.4 (L6426-L6436).

Authority check: Confirmed STORE_POLICY is accurate because splitting an inherited COUNT-bounded series into an UNTIL-bounded prior component and a COUNT-(N-k) future component (while respecting explicit replacement RRULE counts as-is) is a store policy built on RFC 5545's RECURRENCE-ID boundary semantics.
